subject: Evaluation acceptance & close playbook — conformance rubric for pilot
messages:
From: Alyssa Park <alyssa.park@acmehealth.com>
To: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Acme Health Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot evaluation: acceptance criteria and timeline

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo last week. The execs liked the latency and privacy controls; procurement has asked for a concise list of acceptance tests and the minimal pass/fail gates we will use during the 6-week pilot. They want to understand exactly what success looks like before signing the SOW.

High level asks from our side:
- Concrete performance thresholds (99p latency, tokens/sec)
- Accuracy/quality checks for our triage workflows (sample prompts + expected outcomes)
- Data residency and audit log verification steps
- A short plan for fallback behavior if performance regresses

Can you send a short playbook (1–2 pages) that we can review with procurement and the clinical leads? Ideally we get this by next Thursday (6/10) so their legal team can align with the SOW.

—Alyssa
Alyssa Park
Director of Digital Transformation | Acme Health
From: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alyssa Park <alyssa.park@acmehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Jun 2026 12:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot evaluation: acceptance criteria and timeline

Hi Alyssa — thanks for the clear asks. I put together a short decision canvas and acceptance rubric that maps your items to measurable tests and recommended pass thresholds. Overview below; I attached the working MAP spreadsheet and a printable acceptance rubric PDF.

What I included (summary):
1) Performance gates — we propose 99th percentile response time <= 450ms for single-turn triage prompts; median generation cost target and tokens/sec per replica for throughput tests.
2) Quality checks — a 100-sample blind evaluation set from your triage logs, scored for correctness/recall; threshold >= 92% on primary labels, no critical false negatives in >1% of samples.
3) Security/compliance checks — successful ingestion + KMS key rotation validation; end-to-end audit log verification for 48 hours of replay.
4) Availability/fallback — automatic variant routing to a quantized model with degraded quality but <2x latency increase; documented rollback plan and canary window.

Proposed timeline (high level):
- Week 0: kickoff, access + credentials, sample log export
- Week 1: baseline run and smoke tests
- Weeks 2–4: controlled evaluation (sampleed scoring + perf sweeps)
- Week 5: remediation and tuning (if needed)
- Week 6: sign-off window and SOW final review

Next steps: If this looks good I will loop in Karthik to confirm the SLAs we can commit to under Dedicated versus hosted, and Marissa/Ben will own the quality scoring plan. Can review live on Thursday 6/3 or I can send the PDF now for review.

Attaching: MAP-v1.xlsx, pilot-acceptance-rubric.pdf

Best,
Priyom Das
Sr. Solutions Lead — Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Jun 2026 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: scoring buckets and sample selection (Acme pilot)

Quick internal note before I send back to Alyssa — a couple of things we should tighten in the rubric:
- Break the 100-sample set into stratified buckets: emergent (20), high-priority triage (40), low-priority (40). That helps stakeholder signoff.
- Add an explicit regression tolerance: if any single clinical path drops >5% vs baseline, trigger a pause and root cause step.
- For perf tests, include cold-start median and long-tail token growth for the 95->99p window.

Ben — can you draft a short scoring template (CSV) we can include in the MAP so Acme can run the first annotation pass? I will prepare the language to set expectations for remediation windows.

Marissa
Director, GTM Success | Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Jun 2026 11:09:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: scoring buckets and sample selection (Acme pilot)

Attached is the scoring template (CSV stub) and a short rubric note — I included columns for: sample_id, triage_path, expected_label, annotator_label, confidence, review_flag, notes. Sample CSV rows are included as examples.

Couple of clarifications to call out for the external doc:
- We should require Acme to provide the 100-sample export in a sanitized CSV with original prompt, anonymized PHI, and a short context field.
- For the regression trigger, make the action list explicit: 1) notify stakeholder, 2) enter 72-hour tuning window, 3) if unresolved, switch routing to conservative variant and extend pilot by up to 2 weeks at no additional cost (to be negotiated).

I'll push the CSV and a one-page scoring guide to the MAP spreadsheet.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
From: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alyssa Park <alyssa.park@acmehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2026 15:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Final: Acme pilot conformance rubric + next steps (MAP deliverable)

Hi Alyssa — attaching the finalized playbook and a short decision canvas to take to procurement and clinical leadership. Key highlights (TL;DR):

Acceptance gates (must pass all):
- Performance: 99p latency <= 450ms for single-turn triage on Dedicated tier (or <= 650ms hosted fallback).
- Quality: 100-sample blind test with stratified buckets; overall label match >= 92% and no single clinical path < 87%.
- Security: KMS encryption validated, audit log replay successfully reproduces 48 hours of events.
- Resilience: Canary deployment and automatic routing to conservative model if regression >5% for a clinical path.

If any gate fails we enact the remediation sequence: immediate notification -> 72-hour tuning window -> if unresolved, conservative routing + optional 2-week extension. Those terms are captured in the attached MAP spreadsheet and noted for SOW.

Proposed signoff cadence:
- Friday 6/11: Acme internal review of attached rubric and MAP
- Tue 6/15: joint readout with clinical leads (30 min)
- Week of 6/22: expected SOW signature if gates are met

Links: HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/ACM-2026-042) | Shared MAP (https://drive.google.com/open?id=1A2B3C-pilot-plan)

Please confirm whether procurement wants the SOW to explicitly call-out the remediation extension language; we can insert a short clause. Happy to run the readout next Tuesday if that helps.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this live.

Best,
Priyom Das
Sr. Solutions Lead — Redwood Inference
Attachments: MAP-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), pilot-acceptance-rubric.pdf (one-page)
